answer: To deter Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by locking cryptographic stake scaled by C(n)=k*n^2. Each added identity burns stake superlinearly: deploying a sensor in an orchard incurs baseline fees, expanding to a harbor jetty squares the penalty, and swarming a frozen tundra triggers exponential burns. This mathematical cost scaling creates insurmountable economic friction, ensuring attacking costs grow faster than returns.
